frames.slice_level: Upper thorax, at or just above the aortic arch (approximately T2-T4). Trachea round and midline; no arch contour resolved.
Carina / proximal main bronchi, approximately T5-T6. Airway seen centrally as a transverse lucency at the bifurcation.
Below the carina, at the main bronchi / bronchus intermedius, approximately T6-T7. Both bronchi visible as paired lucencies within the mediastinum.
Lower thorax at heart level, approximately T7-T8. Heart occupies most of the mediastinum; bronchus intermedius and left lower lobe bronchus visible as paired lucencies.
Lower thorax approaching the lung bases, approximately T8-T9. Heart occupies the central mediastinum; both lower lobes broadly in view.

cases.impression: Five contiguous axial levels of an unenhanced chest CT on soft-tissue window, descending from the upper thorax to the lung bases. The upper three levels are unremarkable. The lower two demonstrate an extensive heterogeneous abnormality of the right lower lobe: irregular opacity containing multiple small rounded and tubular air-density lucencies, on a background of coarse reticular and branching lines, extending from the perihilar region laterally and posteriorly. The corresponding left lower lobe territory is comparatively spared, and this asymmetry is now clear rather than marginal. This supersedes the frame 4 read, where the same process was visible only as a nodular cluster and was attributed to crowded normal vasculature: the internal air-density lucencies seen at this level are not a vascular finding. The abnormality is definitely present; its nature is not settled by these frames. Bronchiectasis with mucus plugging and consolidation with air bronchograms are the leading considerations, with fibrotic change less likely given the asymmetry. Elsewhere the lungs are aerated with no pneumothorax and no large pleural collection at the levels imaged. Airway patent and midline throughout. Heart occupies the central mediastinum without a discrete mass; chamber size and pericardium are not assessable unenhanced. Bones intact throughout. This warrants review of the actual study on a lung window rather than any conclusion from these screenshots.

findings.location: right lower lobe, extending from the perihilar region laterally and posteriorly
